comparison_markers: ## Upstream Delta Since the Previous Pin

delta_decisions.rationale: DirectML serialization, EmbeddingGemma2/media and model-wrapper changes belong to upstream embedding owners. The fork keeps canonical CPU MiniLM/FastEmbed provenance and model/dimension checks; no model, media interface, accelerator or benchmark claim changes. Any model change retains the independent code/text gates.

Merge history integrates the behavior groups below. Remerge resolutions in palace writes, normalization, search, backend helpers and filesystem helpers were inspected with Git; they are assessed at the final frozen source rather than treated as independent features. No merge or history contract is imported.

The fork has normalized LanceDB vectors and its own deterministic code ranking. Upstream multi-backend cosine scales, closet boosts, BM25 union/ties and timezone/date-window contracts are not the same interface. No ranking migration, benchmark equivalence or new time-filter capability is claimed.

Upstream source formats, registry rows, quick-check shortcuts, general-mode rewrites and media/daemon forwarding differ from fork scanner and generated-copy policy. Exact source replacement is assessed separately; no broad parser or ingest-version migration is imported.

Chroma/raw-SQLite, sqlite_exact, Rust, remote backend filters/vector validation and backend-specific stored-text escaping have no corresponding current storage backend in this LanceDB-only package. The fork does not gain those dependencies or backend contracts.

Upstream capability refactoring, HTTP locks/tokens, light PQL facade, revision logs and tunnel bookkeeping are separate owners and interfaces. The fork retains its typed stdio registry and no update_drawer/revision-log or HTTP service. Shared argument-validation safety is assessed in its own group; no blanket protocol equivalence is claimed.

The fork has its own configuration, atomic publication and lock owners. Upstream shared fsio, Windows retry, alternate YAML naming, environment parser and path consolidation are not copied wholesale. Existing invalid-registry and backup/restore refusal evidence remains scoped to its actual owners, without claiming equivalent behavior for every upstream state file.

The projects have independent release versions, Python ranges, lint rules, Docker/native artifacts and CI. Upstream3.12.0 requires Python3.10; this fork retains its reviewed3.11-3.14 matrix. Upstream export/removed onboarding information updates the comparison only and does not change fork commands.

Upstream closets, AAAK collections, wing aliases/splitting, format miners, persistent tunnels and short-drawer dedup retirement are not imported. Fork cleanup keeps its manual/unique data protections and receipt-bound migration. New upstream maintenance semantics do not authorize deletion or reorganization here.

The fork exposes stdio MCP and local watcher ownership, without upstream hub, daemon forwarding, HTTP proxy or mesh. Upstream token/proxy/browser and process-routing changes have no such reachable surface in this release.

Upstream hook interpreter routing, asynchronous checkpointing and Hermes diary ownership are outside the fork default code-question workflow. This review neither enables conversation persistence nor changes global client instructions or hook installation.

The fork reproduced silent entity-name collisions at its legacy normalized IDs. Its existing KG owner now refuses distinct names before writes, import, invalidation and name-scoped reads, with transaction and snapshot guards. Existing IDs and schema stay unchanged. Upstream punctuation-preserving new IDs and property-merge semantics are not imported; the pre-existing add_entity property-replacement contract remains separate.

The fork uses per-source content hashes, explicit decoding refusal and its own transcript rendering/chunking contracts. Upstream branch selection, transform stamps, multipart rendering and cross-file conversation migration are not asserted as identical. No conversation corpus was inspected or re-mined for this review.

The fork has no upstream LLM client, closet generator or OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint. Upstream now defaults its LLM client to local Ollama and requires consent for external endpoints; API credentials are not intrinsic to local reranking. No external-model feature is added.

The fork already resolves its palace-owned SQLite KG through open_palace_kg and a guarded legacy-adoption owner. Upstream graph-selection and import-conflict policy are different durable contracts; automatic graph switching, merging and a new import command are not added. The confirmed name collision in the local adoption path is fixed in the separate preservation group.

The fork already validates required strings, booleans, enums, ranges, text bounds, unknown arguments and sanitized handler failures in its dispatcher. Its existing real stdio regressions exercise refusal and continued service. No upstream coercion or network-token contract is copied.

The fork add_drawers_batch delegates changed-source replacement to one LanceDB composite merge. Failure leaves old source rows and manual rows outside the replacement scope. Existing source-failure and storage merge regressions are the evidence; upstream closet/AAAK cleanup contracts are absent.

Upstream now carries stray bytes and records transforms through its own wire/storage paths. The fork refuses undecodable sources instead of filing replacement characters. A reversible stored-text representation would change its durable contract and requires separate acceptance; no such migration is introduced.

The fork already passes spellcheck=False for supported conversation mining and preserves code identifiers. Upstream opt-in spell correction and transform stamps are not enabled; the existing local predicates establish the refusal to silently spell-correct.
